prompt: A small business models its daily profit with $P(x) = 8.5x - 240$, where $x$ is the number of items sold and $P$ is profit in dollars. What does the $x$-intercept of this function represent?

choices.label: The profit made when no items are sold
The number of items that must be sold to break even
The profit earned on each item sold
The maximum number of items that can be sold

hint: The $x$-intercept is where the output is zero. What does zero profit mean here?

hints.text: The $x$-intercept is where the output is zero. What does zero profit mean here?

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try it with tiny numbers: $P(x) = 2x - 6$. The $x$-intercept is $x = 3$, and selling 3 items yields exactly $\$0$ profit — costs covered, nothing more. That is break-even.
Zero profit means revenue exactly covers costs — that is the break-even point.
It is the number of items sold at which profit is $\$0$: break even.

learningObjective: Interpret the x-intercept of a linear model in context.
explanation: The $x$-intercept is the value of $x$ making $P(x) = 0$.
Zero profit means the business has covered its costs exactly and made nothing beyond them — the break-even point.

Choice A describes the $y$-intercept ($-\$240$, a loss) and choice C describes the slope ($\$8.50$ per item). Every one of the wrong answers is a correct statement about a *different* feature of the model.

alternativeExplanations.title: Compute it and read the number
steps: Selling 28 items still leaves a small loss; 29 turns the first profit.
A number like "about 28 items" only makes sense as a break-even count — the arithmetic itself rules the other choices out.
